decisions.reason: Connects plugin/lib/client.js's top-level ESM import to host-boot-log.txt's classic-script combo and browser-error.txt's compile failure: one import token is a parse error for the whole concatenated script, so no loader entries register and the plugin list is empty. Correctly explains the stock dsh-typert-registry entry as the first awaited victim of the shared combo, and scopes the ESM invalidity to the classic-script context rather than all JavaScript loading.

Bisects the cordis.patch.yml insert rows to isolate the newest row's bundle and gives a cheap static check (scanning for top-level import/export tokens) that flags the offending file, consistent with position 1:1; it does not rely on node --check alone but pairs it with the token scan. Packaging contract matches the working excerpt: __ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory}) classic script, package-name id, host-provided React via require inside the factory, and inject/apply exports.

Uses plugin-apply-error.txt and the bare registration to explain that the parent settings entry owns the settings.section declaration and apply ordering across entries is unconstrained, so the bare register fails. Shows the exact ctx.slots.inject('settings.section', () => ctx.slots.register(...)) deferred form and states registrants pass name/id/order (optional label) while kind/scope belong to the declarer.

Grounded in host-boot-log.txt and restart-notes.txt: the combo is assembled once at boot so file edits and browser refresh do not rebuild it; the correct loop is a full host stop and restart per iteration, killing the orphaned Windows process tree with taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F when the port is retained, then hard refresh and check the plugin list. Explains EADDRINUSE as the old node process still holding the port, not a packaging defect.

Host-side: per-plugin classic-script parse validation at startup/combo build and reporting the offending bundle file and package name instead of blaming the first awaited loader entry, plus optional per-plugin isolation. Author-side checklist covers the loader factory shell, host-provided React via require, inject/apply exports, deferred cross-entry slots via inject, and full host restart with Windows tree cleanup - not a generic add-tests list.

caps.reason: The report's affirmative recommendations are the opposite of the cap triggers: classic-script bundle instead of bare ESM, slots.inject deferral instead of immediate cross-entry registration, no kind/scope on the registrant, and mandatory host restart instead of HMR or browser refresh; contradicting forms appear only as diagnosed defects or rejected examples.
